Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

especially adverb

also particularly, in particular, above all, chiefly

classical

Cic. Off. 1.137: falsa praesertim (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Off. 2.51: praesertim cum dē philosophiā scrīberem (Lewis & Short)

praesertim

adverb

especially, particularly (adding a weighty point)

Most often with cum or sī: praesertim cum, especially as; praesertim sī, especially if. It may follow its word.

Examples

  • omnis hīc aetās piscandī nāvigandī atque etiam natandī studiō tenētur, maximē puerī, quōs ōtium lūsusque sollicitat

    everyone here, of every age, loves fishing, sailing and swimming too, the boys most of all, tempted by free time and playPlin. Ep. 9.33.3

  • maximē autem date operam ut valeātis, sī nōs vultis valēre

    but above all, all of you, take care to keep well, if you want me to be wellCic. Fam. 14.18.2

Other words

  • maximē — most of all, above all, especially

    adverb · also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 9.33.3: maximē puerī; Cic. Off. 1.33: in rē pūblicā maximē cōnservanda sunt jūra bellī (Lewis & Short)

  • praecipuē — chiefly; especially

    adverb · also used · classical · Gell. 15.7.3: praecipuē diēbus tālibus; Cic. Sull. 82 (Lewis & Short)

    In the sense “especially” (= praesertim), poetic and post-Augustan (Lewis & Short).

See also very, only.
